rule: Call through a parameter, local variable or stored property holding a function (callback, closure, fn pointer, delegate) -> callee is the variable's name, `call_type` callback, confidence unknown. | Not calls: passing a method reference (`x::m`, `self.m` without call), ... field access without a call.
notes: Each `require` is an invocation of the loader: `_G#require`, medium, direct, on its line (Decisions 2026-11-10, CommonJS / Lua `require`). main.lua is not itself required; it sits at the require root (src/) that explains every require string in the case, so the name a require from that root gives it is `main` (Lua note: 'module = the name the scan's `require` strings give the file'). call_type convention (SPEC lists the types but gives no Lua mapping): a `:` call is method, a `.` or bare call is direct (the 2026-11-10 require ruling makes `_G#require` direct), a call through a value is callback. `handler` is a parameter; `h` is a local holding `handler or default_handler` (an expression, not an alias of one function, so the alias decision does not apply); `fn` is a local holding a call result. All three are calls through values: callee = variable name, callback, unknown. Passing `E.compare` to table.sort, reading it into `ref`, storing it in a table constructor, `#list`, `t.n`, and passing `print` as an argument are references/field access/operators, not calls. `E` is the returned table, so functions are `events#...`.
